correctness.rationale: For \(n\ge5\), the cubic degree condition and two triple configurations rule out three-vertex forcing. Exhausting the possible fourth vertex after the first force yields precisely eight configurations, which reduce to five disjoint symmetry orbits; each representative completes two neighboring rungs and hence forces the entire cylinder. Orbit stabilizers of orders \(2,1,1,4,2\) prove the exact \(13n\) count. The included verifier exhaustively compares all four-subsets at orders 5 through 15 with the orbit construction and checks all three-subsets there; these finite calculations corroborate but do not prove the uniform statement.

value.rationale: The first nonzero coefficient of the zero forcing polynomial counts all initial conditions of optimal cardinality and is a natural graph invariant explicitly motivated by Boyer et al. A five-orbit classification explains its nonobvious linear growth \(13n\) for an infinite family of cubic Hamiltonian graphs. Determining optimizer multiplicity and structure is substantively stronger than reporting only the known numerical zero forcing threshold; the result does not claim the entire polynomial.
